overview: Totonac histories belong to a diverse region of Veracruz and Puebla. Cempoala offers one documented example of urban institutions, agriculture and water engineering.

items.text: Agriculture supported regional settlements. At Cempoala, production areas lay both inside and outside the dispersed city.
Cempoala used protective walls against flooding and channels to supply the city. Drains carried household and building wastewater toward cultivated areas.
Cempoala combined plazas and temples with different plans, including a circular temple associated with Ehecatl.
At Yohualichan, niches are interpreted by INAH as references to local caves. Shared architectural features do not prove one homogeneous state.
Cempoala became a tributary center under Mexica domination. In 1519 its ruler allied with Cortés against Tenochtitlan.
INAH describes continuing regional language, food, dances and festivities. Totonac culture cannot be reduced to the disappearance of a precolonial city.

sources.title: J. Omar Ruiz Gordillo, INAH: Cultura Totonaca
